findings.summary_md: WorkOS disclosed that on October 30, 2026 it identified unauthorized access to an internal sales-team application. The accessed data included business contact details, customer account histories, summaries of sales and support communications, and product usage metadata. The bulletin states the attacker used an AI-assisted offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation, and says external access to the app was disabled while an independent forensics firm was retained.
findings.title: October 30th, 2026 Data Security Incident

findings.summary_md: First news coverage of the WorkOS breach reported that founder Michael Grinich attributed the intrusion to the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite, an open-source project by Chinese developers that later went private after use against South Korean banks. The report notes investigators found user-agent strings `artex-enrich/1.0` and `norma/0.4` in attacker web requests, and cites prior ARTEX-linked activity including a CrowdStrike-reported campaign against 200 organizations and an attack on the DIVD non-profit.
findings.title: WorkOS says attacker used ARTEX AI to breach internal sales app

findings.summary_md: AhnLab ASEC published an analysis using ARTEX as its case study for AI-driven autonomous penetration testing, describing systems in which LLM agents chain planning, tool execution, and result analysis across interconnected steps. The report places ARTEX alongside tools such as Vulnhuntr and GhidraMCP and describes ASEC's investigation of exposed ARTEX-related web services, including AI API gateways and attack-surface tooling. It predates the WorkOS incident by over three weeks and documents that ARTEX infrastructure was already visible to defenders.
findings.title: The Threat of AI-Driven Autonomous Penetration Testing, as Examined by ARTEX
